theme: 3 terms on how Auto Layout shares space: the natural size a view gets from its content, the priority against growing, and the priority against shrinking

terms.definition: The natural size a view wants from its own content, like the width of a label's text.
terms.example: A label has an Intrinsic Content Size, so it only needs a position, not a width.

terms.definition: A priority for how strongly a view refuses to grow bigger than its natural content size.
terms.example: Raise the badge's Content Hugging, so the title label takes the extra space.

terms.definition: A priority for how strongly a view refuses to shrink smaller than its natural content size.
terms.example: Bump the price label's Compression Resistance, so the name gets cut instead.
terms.code:
// the price must never be cut
let p = priceLabel
p.setContentCompressionResistancePriority(
    .required, for: .horizontal)

video.title: Intrinsic Content Size, Content Hugging & Compression Resistance | Day 85
video.description:
Learn to explain how Auto Layout decides which view grows or shrinks: Intrinsic Content Size, Content Hugging & Compression Resistance, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Intrinsic Content Size - The natural size a view wants from its own content, like the width of a label's text.
Content Hugging - A priority for how strongly a view refuses to grow bigger than its natural content size.
Compression Resistance - A priority for how strongly a view refuses to shrink smaller than its natural content size.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

Explain Intrinsic Content Size, Content Hugging & Compression Resistance in UIKit by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.

Intrinsic Content Size - The natural size a view wants from its own content, like the width of a label's text.
한국어: 고유 콘텐츠 크기: 레이블의 텍스트 너비처럼, 뷰가 자기 콘텐츠로부터 원하는 자연스러운 크기

Content Hugging - A priority for how strongly a view refuses to grow bigger than its natural content size.
한국어: 콘텐츠 허깅: 뷰가 자연스러운 콘텐츠 크기보다 커지기를 얼마나 강하게 거부하는지 나타내는 우선순위

Compression Resistance - A priority for how strongly a view refuses to shrink smaller than its natural content size.
한국어: 압축 저항: 뷰가 자연스러운 콘텐츠 크기보다 작아지기를 얼마나 강하게 거부하는지 나타내는 우선순위

landscape.hook: Two labels, one row, and the price gets cut. Can you explain why in English?

dialogue.title: Who gets cut off?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, the `price` gets cut off when the product `name` is long.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Both labels want their Intrinsic Content Size, and there isn't room.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So Auto Layout has to shrink one of them?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Right. It checks Compression Resistance to decide which one gives up space.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then both use the same default, so Auto Layout can pick either one.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So I raise Compression Resistance on `price`?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. Then `name` shrinks and shows dots at the end.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: What if the name is short? Which label stretches?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's Content Hugging. Give `price` higher Content Hugging, so it stays tight.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Got it. `price` keeps its Intrinsic Content Size, and `name` takes the rest.

dialogue.code:
NSLayoutConstraint.activate([
    price.leadingAnchor.constraint(
        equalTo: name.trailingAnchor),
    price.trailingAnchor.constraint(
        equalTo: card.trailingAnchor)
])
